title: Force-on-Force Readiness
metaDescription: Force-on-force exercise design and readiness assessment that validates the protective strategy under realistic, controlled conditions.
heroDek: A protective strategy is a hypothesis until it's exercised. GSS designs and assesses force-on-force exercises grounded in the site's own analysis, then closes the loop on what the results show.
contextHeading: A protective strategy is a hypothesis until it's exercised
contextParagraphs: Force-on-force exercises test detection, delay, and response under controlled, realistic mock-adversary conditions. They exist to close the loop on the analysis performed earlier, such as pathway and timeline analysis and response strategy development, by confirming, or challenging, what that analysis predicted.

GSS designs exercise scenarios directly from the site's own Design Basis Threat, target sets, and timeline analysis rather than from an arbitrary or convenient scenario, and assesses protective-force readiness beforehand so the exercise measures the strategy itself, not an unprepared force standing in for it.

Results are analyzed against the original timeline and response-strategy assumptions and fed back into revisions of the response strategy, barrier validation priorities, and the training program that produced the force being exercised.

methodology.label: Readiness Assessment
methodology.body: Protective force and equipment readiness evaluated before exercise design begins.

methodology.label: Scenario Design
methodology.body: Exercise scenarios developed from the site's own Design Basis Threat, target sets, and timeline analysis.

methodology.label: Safety & Control Planning
methodology.body: Exercise safety controls and umpiring protocols established before execution.

methodology.label: Exercise Execution
methodology.body: Scenario run under controlled, monitored conditions with mock-adversary and response-force participation.

methodology.label: Performance Data Collection
methodology.body: Timeline, engagement, and communication performance recorded through the exercise.

methodology.label: After-Action Analysis
methodology.body: Results analyzed against the original timeline and response-strategy assumptions and fed back into revision.

faq.q: Are exercise scenarios generic, or site-specific?
faq.a: Grounded in the site's own Design Basis Threat, target sets, and timeline analysis, not an arbitrary or off-the-shelf scenario.

faq.q: What happens to the results afterward?
faq.a: After-action analysis feeds directly back into response strategy revision, barrier validation priorities, and the training program.

faq.q: Does GSS assess readiness before the exercise, or only after?
faq.a: Both. A pre-exercise readiness assessment comes first, then performance data collection during and after the exercise itself.

ctaHeading: Test the strategy under control, before something else tests it
